blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 370 and Article 35A historically defined the special status and constitutional relationship of J&K with India.
Key provisions were abrogated on August 5, 2019, reshaping the state's political structure.
The J&K Reorganisation Act 2019 provides the current administrative and legal framework.
The Delimitation Commission in 2022 redrew electoral constituencies for the UT of J&K.
Article 370 gave special status to J&K under Indian Constitution
Under Art 370, Parliament could legislate on J&K only on Defence, Foreign Affairs, Finance & Communications (as per Instrument of Accession)
All other laws needed J&K government's concurrence
J&K had its own Constitution (1956), flag, and Penal Code (Ranbir Penal Code — RPC)
President's Rule could not be imposed under Art 356; instead Art 370 had separate provisions
Inserted by Presidential Order 1954 (under Art 370)
Empowered J&K legislature to define 'Permanent Residents' and give them exclusive rights to property, government jobs, and scholarships
Non-state subjects could not buy land or settle permanently in J&K
President Ram Nath Kovind issued Constitutional Order 272 (2019) rendering Art 370 inoperative
Rajya Sabha passed J&K Reorganisation Act on August 5; Lok Sabha on August 6, 2019
Art 35A automatically lapsed with Art 370
J&K lost statehood; became UT with legislature
Ladakh separated; became UT without legislature (like Chandigarh)
Supreme Court (Dec 2023): Upheld abrogation of Art 370 as constitutionally valid
SC directed restoration of statehood to J&K 'at earliest'

cells: UT with Legislature (like Delhi/Puducherry); has elected Legislative Assembly
UT without Legislature (like Chandigarh/Andaman); governed directly by Centre through LG
Head of UT; appointed by President; executive authority
Head of elected govt; real executive in matters under legislature
90 seats (after delimitation 2022); 7 reserved for STs, 9 for SCs
LAHDC Leh & LAHDC Kargil — elected bodies for local governance in Ladakh

items: Divided former J&K into two UTs: J&K (with legislature) and Ladakh (without legislature)
Leh and Kargil districts → Ladakh UT
All 18 remaining districts (then) → J&K UT
IPS, IAS, IFS officers: cadre reorganized; new J&K cadre and AGMUT cadre for Ladakh
Ranbir Penal Code (RPC) replaced by Indian Penal Code (IPC)
J&K Civil Services replaced by J&K Administrative Service (JKAS)
Central laws extended to J&K that were earlier excluded

blocks.content: 3.4 Important Constitutional Provisions for J&K UT

items: Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas) now applicable to tribal areas of J&K
RTI Act applicable since 2019
RTE Act applicable since 2019
National Commission for Women applicable
CAG can audit J&K finances
NIA (National Investigation Agency) jurisdiction extended to J&K
PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act) applicable
Set up under Delimitation Act 2002; chaired by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai (retd.)
J&K Assembly: Increased from 83 to 90 seats
Jammu: 37 → 43 seats (6 more); Kashmir: 46 → 47 seats (1 more)
9 seats reserved for SCs; 7 seats reserved for STs (for first time)
Kashmiri migrants (Pandits) given representation in Assembly (2 seats nominated)
Delimitation based on 2011 census

cells: Constitutional body; recruits gazetted officers; conducts KAS, KPS exams
Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council — Leh; established 1995
Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council — Kargil; established 2003
3-tier system; Panchayats, Block Dev. Councils, District Dev. Councils in J&K UT
Established 2020; 14-member elected district-level bodies; first elections Dec 2020

items: Remember the key landmark date for the abrogation of Article 370: August 5, 2019.
Understand the statutory provisions introduced under the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019.
Be prepared for questions on the 2022 Delimitation Commission's role in electoral restructuring.

cells: Founded 1932 by Sheikh Abdullah; dominant in Kashmir; recently won 2024 elections
Founded 1999 by Mufti Mohammad Sayeed; strong in south Kashmir

items: PM Gram Sadak Yojana: All-weather roads to villages
PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana): Housing for all
NREGA/MGNREGS: Employment guarantee
Aspirational Districts Program: Several J&K districts covered
Back to Village Program (B2V): J&K government initiative; officials visit panchayats
My Town My Pride: Urban version of B2V
Industrial Policy 2021-30: Rs 28,400 crore investment target; incentives for industries
'Dil, Diya, Dehleez' — LG Manoj Sinha's governance programme
Mission Youth: Youth empowerment programme in J&K
UNDP collaboration: SDG alignment in J&K
